sections.title: DISCUSSION
sections.text:
Issued at 138 AM EDT Wed Sep 23 2026

Here in southern Appalachia, we're getting another bout of homegrown 
showers and thunderstorms today. A diving trough cutting to the 
southeast underneath a Rex block will combine a good vort max, some 
mild upper divergence, and warm and moist air to produce another 
round of scattered to numerous thunderstorms later today. Effective 
shear is present underneath all that, around 20 knots, deep layer 
shear a little stronger, so depending on the storms it's possible 
there's one or two severe storms for wind gusts, though I'm not as 
sold on a severe hail risk. Otherwise storm motions are forecast to 
be near 10 knots, so slow moving storms do present a risk for flash 
flooding, especially if on previously saturated soils or vulnerable 
soils. Both 00z REFS and 00z HREF depict heavy rain swaths enough to 
induce flash flooding in the mountain counties south of Knoxville 
for today, but I wouldn't take the exact locations as gospel. 
Thursday skinny and somewhat shallow vertical profiles will still 
support a few showers, with perhaps more scattered light rain under 
the still moist atmosphere.

Chattanooga. Congratulations. After 50 days of 90F or hotter 
weather, you have attained the next part of the year: still warm but 
not excruciatingly hot. Possibly even more shocking are the low 
temperatures, after 100+ days of minimums being 60F or greater, 
Chattanooga will hit the 50s beginning this weekend. 

GFS/Euro are in agreement that we'll be on the backside of a solid 
nor'easter on the Eastern seaboard this weekend, which means we'll 
be on the receiving end of dry continental air while that storm 
system matures off the New England coast. Might have a few 
overperforming radiation nights this weekend in Virginia, skies look 
to be clear in the low PWAT environment with very dry air present. 
It is conceivable that a few colder hollows might get into, gasp, 
the upper 30s Saturday and Sunday mornings! First taste of fall has 
arrived. Daytime afternoon RH values are likely to lead to a very 
pleasant weekend, which is the best benefit from dry air plus still 
mildly warm temperatures.

MVFR to IFR cigs will continue to expand into region overnight.
The combination of low cigs and some light wind should be enough
to prevent much dense fog from forming. MVFR cigs look to stick
around through early afternoon before they scatter out. Another
round of showers and storms will develop in the afternoon and
evening hours. Maintained the PROB30s given the uncertainty with
coverage.

enso.title: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory
paragraphs: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory Synopsis: El Niño is strengthening, with a greater than 90% chance of a very strong event during the Northern Hemisphere fall and winter 2026-27. El Niño strengthened further over the past month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +3.0°C in the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Except for the Niño-4 index, which decreased to +0.1°C in August, values in the other Niño indices increased, reaching +1.8°C in Niño-3.4, +2.5°C in Niño-3, and +3.4°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) remained steady during August [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline [Fig. 4] . Subsurface temperatures continued to be significantly above average, with widespread anomalies in excess of +10.0°C at depth. Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies extended from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices remained negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6

-8] . During the October-December 2026 season, there is a 75% chance of a historic event that would exceed the strength of previous El Niño events dating back to 1950 (+2.5°C or more for a 3-month RONI value ). With an event of this magnitude, the chances of experiencing impacts consistent with El Niño are larger, though not guaranteed (see CPC outlooks for probabilities of seasonal anomalies). In summary, El Niño is strengthening, with a greater than 90% chance of a very strong event during the Northern Hemisphere fall and winter 2026-27. This discussion is a consolidated effort of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), NOAA's National Weather Service, and their funded institutions. md.summary: Marginally severe hail and isolated severe gusts are possible this afternoon. Overall severe coverage should remain too limited for a watch.
md.discussion: A compact upper low is evident on water vapor imagery along northern portions of the Utah/Nevada border. Lift from this feature is promoting scattered convection across northern/eastern portions of the Great Basin this afternoon. Some activity near the Great Salt Lake has intensified during the last half hour. With additional heating, other storms may similarly increase in strength. The strongest shear exists in eastern Utah/western Colorado where the mid-level jet core is located. However, these areas have remained cooler/less unstable. Severe potential will likely be maximized along the northwest periphery of the mid-level jet where MLCAPE has risen to 500-750 J/kg. Temperatures near the upper low are cold enough to support marginally severe hail despite weaker shear. Isolated severe gusts are also possible.
